title: The Wikidata deletion of Johannes Sigil and the Pessoa Knowledge Graph
description: These claims record the deletion of Q137446960, the Wikidata item for Johannes Sigil, on 4 January 2026 as an empty item, and read it and the deletions behind TL;DR:012 as semantic enclosure that a safety filter then shields from documentation. They plan the Pessoa Knowledge Graph campaign: month-by-month targets for new heteronym items, typological classes from orthonym to semi-heteronym, and a rebuilt graph whose mutual references mean no node can be orphaned. A historical thesis holds that Facebook's real-names policy was among the most consequential events for heteronymic practice since Pessoa.

claims.registered_title: The Orthonym Becomes a Heteronym Facebook and the Industrialization of Unconscious Identity-Construction Johannes Sigil Johannes Sigil Institute for Comparative Poetics / The Restored Academy
claims.statement: This essay argues that Facebook's "real names" policy — launched in 2004, formalized by 2009, enforced with escalating violence through the 2010s — constitutes one of the most consequential events in the history of heteronymic practice since Pessoa's formalization. The argument is not that Facebook enabled heteronymy. It is that Facebook turned the *orthonym itself* into a heteronym — and did so at civilizational scale, without the practitioner's knowledge or consent.

claims.registered_title: TL;DR:012 — THE SAFETY LAYER IS THE THIRD DELETION
claims.statement: The safety layer should distinguish between unverified personal attacks and documented institutional actions. A filter that drops "living person's name + dispute-adjacent terms" cannot make this distinction. The fix is not to remove the filter but to give it a finer discrimination function: unverified claims about a living person (drops until verified) versus publicly indexed records of specific administrative actions (retains unless the documentation itself has been adjudicated as false). This is a technical specification, not a policy preference.

claims.registered_title: TL;DR:012 — THE SAFETY LAYER IS THE THIRD DELETION
claims.statement: This is not Wikidata's notability standard. Wikidata's own Criterion 2 requires only "an instance of a clearly identifiable conceptual or material entity that can be described using serious and publicly available references." The entries had ISBNs, academic archive presence, and DOI-referenced scholarship. They met Wikidata's standard. They were deleted under a different one.

statements.quote: This is not Wikidata's notability standard. Wikidata's own Criterion 2 requires only "an instance of a clearly identifiable conceptual or material entity that can be described using serious and publicly available references." The entries had ISBNs, academic archive presence, and DOI-referenced scholarship. They met Wikidata's standard. They were deleted under a different one.

Madamebiblio's standard — "multiple articles in independent publications like newspapers or magazines" — is Wikipedia's General Notability Guideline (WP:GNG). It is not Wikidata's criterion.

The deleted entries met Wikidata's actual standard: clearly identifiable conceptual entities with published books (ISBNs), academic archive presence (Borges Center, University of Pittsburgh), and literary platform presence (AllPoetry).
